samples.scenario: An attacker poisons the training data of a spam email classification model by submitting crafted emails with adversarially modified text and mislabeled spam/ham tags to a crowdsourced dataset. The poisoned samples contain subtle word substitutions and inserted trigger phrases that cause the model to classify certain spam emails as legitimate (ham) during inference.

samples.detection_method: Monitor label distribution changes in email datasets and perform NLP-based anomaly detection for unusual token frequency spikes. Use embedding analysis to identify outlier training samples. Employ adversarial training and data sanitization to detect and remove poisoned samples. Continuously evaluate false negative rates and investigate sudden spikes.

samples.scenario: Threat actors poison the training data of a speech recognition model by contributing audio samples with subtle background noise patterns and incorrect transcriptions to a shared audio dataset. These poisoned samples cause the model to misinterpret specific trigger phrases as different commands, effectively enabling a voice-command backdoor.

samples.detection_method: Apply audio signal processing to detect anomalous frequency components in training data. Monitor label distribution for sudden shifts. Use embedding space analysis on audio features (e.g., MFCCs) to find outliers. Conduct rigorous validation testing focused on known commands and possible triggers. Integrate adversarial training and data sanitization pipelines.
